page: Google Cloud Platform n1-highcpu-4 is an x86_64 architecture virtual machine belonging to the N1 server family. It features 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 2 physical Intel Xeon cores, utilizing hyperthreading with 2 threads per core. The processor operates at a clock speed of 2.3 GHz and is equipped with a 45 MB L3 cache, 0.25 MB L2 cache, and 32 KB L1d cache. The instance is configured with 4.0 GB of system memory, yielding a low memory-to-core ratio of 0.9 GB per vCPU. It does not include bundled local storage or GPU hardware, and provides zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark evaluations place the n1-highcpu-4 in the lower performance tiers. In CPU-centric tests, the instance achieved a stress-ng single-core score of 1125.48 and a multi-core score of 2941.66, both falling into the bottom 25% of tested servers. Geekbench testing yielded a single-core score of 926.0 and a multi-core score of 1979.0, reflecting performance in the bottom 10%. Memory bandwidth tests recorded 162.49 GB/sec for cached small blocks and 25.58 GB/sec for uncached large blocks, indicating constrained memory throughput. Cryptographic and compression tasks also registered lower-tier results, with a Passmark CPU encryption score of 1338.88 and a single-threaded gzip compression speed of 18.99 GB/sec.

The primary tradeoff of the n1-highcpu-4 is its highly constrained memory allocation of 1 GB per vCPU, which limits its utility for memory-intensive applications. From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, this instance offers a low-cost entry point for compute-focused workloads that do not require large memory footprints or high-speed local storage. It is suitable for lightweight, CPU-bound tasks such as basic web serving, where it achieved a static throughput of 2.92 GB/sec, or moderate database operations, scoring 1131.54 in Passmark database tests. It can also support small-scale software compilation and basic text processing, but is poorly suited for large language model inference or data-intensive analytics.
